title: Regular trajectories, pruning and quantum parity
summary: We prove that constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates and unbounded-arity Toffoli gates cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage using polynomially many total qubits. Ancillary qubits are initialized to $`|0\rangle`$, one output qubit is measured, and all other final registers may be discarded without restriction. This resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model.

review.reason: Proves constant-depth quantum circuits cannot compute parity with polynomially many qubits.
